2027-01-26.title: Fourth Tuesday of Denha · Republic Day of India
2027-01-26.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: No prophet is accepted in the prophet's hometown
2027-01-26.alt: Season of Denha. Republic Day of India. Sts Timothy and Titus: 2 Samuel 22:2–4; Wisdom 7:28–8:3; 1 Timothy 6:11–16; Matthew 16:24–27.
2027-01-26.verse: “Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts.”
theo: Hebrews looks back at Israel in the wilderness, who heard God's promise of rest and did not enter it, “because they were not united by faith with those who listened.” The promise has not expired: “while the promise of entering his rest is still open, let us take care that none of you should seem to have failed to reach it.” And God sets a day for us, the same day every day: “Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts.” The Gospel shows what a hardened heart looks like. In the synagogue at Nazareth everyone at first speaks well of Jesus and is amazed at his gracious words; then comes the question, “Is not this Joseph's son?” Familiarity turns to contempt. Jesus answers, “Truly I tell you, no prophet is accepted in the prophet's hometown”, and reminds them that Elijah was sent to a widow in Sidon and Elisha cleansed Naaman the Syrian. God's mercy crosses borders. The townspeople are filled with rage and try to throw him off a cliff, “But he passed through the midst of them and went on his way.”

Today India keeps Republic Day, remembering the Constitution that came into force in 1950, promising justice, liberty, equality and fraternity to all and the freedom to profess, practise and propagate religion. The Gospel speaks to such a day. It is easy to love one's own town and harder to hear the prophet who comes from it; easy to think God belongs to us and harder to rejoice that he blesses the widow of Zarephath and the Syrian general. Christians serve their nation best by listening today to God's voice, by refusing contempt for those they know too well, and by welcoming every neighbour of every faith. The Church also honours Sts Timothy and Titus, the young bishops whom Paul trusted with the churches of Ephesus and Crete. To Timothy he wrote: “Fight the good fight of the faith”. We give thanks for our country, pray for all who govern it, and ask for pastors who, like Timothy and Titus, keep the faith among the people.

Pray for the nation, its Constitution, its leaders, its poor, and harmony among all communities.
2027-01-26.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, in your own hometown you were not accepted, yet you passed through the crowd and went on your way to save us. Soften our hearts to hear your voice today. On this Republic Day bless India with justice, liberty, equality and fraternity, make us good citizens and faithful disciples, and through the prayers of Sts Timothy and Titus give your Church shepherds who fight the good fight of the faith. Amen.
altar: At every Holy Qurbana we hear his voice today in the word, pray for those who govern, as the Church has always done, and receive the rest he promised in his Body and Blood.

2027-01-26.question: Have I stopped listening to someone because I know them too well?

family.explain: Jesus went home to Nazareth. At first people liked his words, but then they said: he is only Joseph's son! They got angry and did not listen. Jesus is God's Son, and we must listen to him every day.
family.intention: We pray for India on Republic Day, and for people of all religions who live together.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone in our family we need to listen to better?”

illus: In a village near Kanjirappally a young engineer came home to start a waste-recycling unit. The elders laughed: we knew him when he ran barefoot in the paddy fields. Only when the district collector praised the project did they listen. At the Republic Day assembly the parish priest read Luke 4 and said: sometimes God's gift is the person we think we know too well.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, today we want to hear your voice. Soften our hearts and bless our nation. Amen.
share: Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts (Hebrews 4:7). Where is my heart hard?
Is not this Joseph's son? (Luke 4:22). Whom do I despise because I know them too well?
He passed through the midst of them and went on his way (Luke 4:30). Do I let Jesus go on his way without me?
interc: For India on Republic Day: for justice, liberty, equality and fraternity.
For the President, the Prime Minister and all who govern.
For religious freedom and harmony among communities.
For bishops, through Sts Timothy and Titus.
For our group, that we may hear God's voice today.
pm.close: Father, your Son was rejected in his own town and still offered salvation to all. Make us listen to him and serve our nation in love. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Hebrews tells us that God's promised rest is still open, and that God sets a day for us: today. Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts (Hebrews 4:7).

At Nazareth the people first admire Jesus' gracious words, then ask: is not this Joseph's son? (Luke 4:22). They think they know him too well to listen. Jesus says: no prophet is accepted in the prophet's hometown (Luke 4:24), and reminds them that God's mercy reached a widow of Sidon and a Syrian general.

Today is Republic Day. Our Constitution promises justice, liberty, equality and fraternity to all. Christians serve this nation by listening to God today, by rejecting contempt, and by welcoming every neighbour of every faith.

We also honour Sts Timothy and Titus, whom Paul told to fight the good fight of the faith (1 Timothy 6:12). Let us thank God for India, pray for those who govern, and keep our hearts soft to his voice. Amen.
kids: Children, the people of Nazareth did not listen to Jesus because they thought he was just Joseph's son. Let us listen to Jesus today, and pray for our country India!

q: Righteousness exalts a nation, but sin is a reproach to any people.

concl: God's today is still open; do not harden your hearts.
Listen to the prophet at home and serve the nation with fraternity.
